name: @everfur/mcp

tools.name: everfur_plan_integration
tools.description: Produce an integration plan for a project. REFUSES underspecified input by naming the missing facts rather than guessing them, and REFUSES a project shape the SDK ships no entry point for (PLATFORM_NOT_SUPPORTED), a React Native app older than the SDK supports, 0.74 (REACT_NATIVE_TOO_OLD: upgrade it), or a capability set the contract blocks outright (CAPABILITIES_BLOCKED). Returns a small summary with a plan_id and a number of pages: the goal, the detected facts, each step's id, title, one-line intent and page, and the checklist. The same arguments plus plan_id and page (1 to pages) return that page: its steps in full, with their commands and the complete body of each file they write, and on page 1 the detection, warnings and checklist in full. With steps (step ids) instead of page, those steps come a page at a time and remaining_steps names the rest. Each call recomputes the plan from the project, which the plan's own commands and files change, so every page is fetched before any command runs or any file is written. Read-only. Reads the contract from GET /partners/contract with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY unless contract_path or EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC names a projection file. It plans the SDK surfaces (chat, records, Televet and the rest) only; an insurer connecting its claims system to Everfur is planned by everfur_plan_claims_integration, which needs no project.

project_root.description: For a local MCP only: absolute path to the application root. Pass exactly one of this or project_details.

project_details.description: For a remote MCP only: a safe projection of package dependencies, package manager, and fixed file-presence markers. Pass exactly one of this or project_root; never send source files, env files, or credentials.

theme_source.description: For a remote MCP: the text of the project's tailwind.config.{js,ts}, the CSS that declares its theme (a Tailwind v4 @theme block or :root custom properties), or a React Native theme or colours file, so the plan can match the generated surface to the project's own theme. Read statically and never executed. With project_root the project is read from disk instead; this argument, when given, wins. The plan refuses to guess a theme it cannot read and names the missing facts in its match-theme step.

capabilities.description: Which Everfur capabilities this integration uses, as the contract names them. The ids the contract can plan today are "chat", "entitlements", "events", "notifications", "photo", "records", "records-clinic" and "televet", and "texting" (the member's opt-in to texts, a human-tap surface) once the loaded contract publishes it as plannable; "animations", "claims", "health-plan", "records-push", "records-transfer", "server-pets" and "video" are blocked today and a plan refuses them with the reason. Pass ["all"] for every plannable capability. The loaded contract is the authority: an UNKNOWN_OPTION refusal lists its exact ids. The plan holds no credential, so everfur_verify_integration (not this tool) is the fail-closed check of what the tenant actually has. The native setup an in-app vet call needs (the Daily modules, an Expo config plugin, a clean prebuild, camera and microphone declarations, and a warning naming the missing-native-module error Expo Go produces) is planned only when the generated React Native file mounts that call; a plan whose file mounts only the vet visit button installs none of it. Omit if unknown; the tool will refuse and list the ids.

identity_mode.description: anonymous = no backend, scoped to the device. partner-user-ref = your backend mints a session against your own user id. shopify-app-proxy = a Shopify storefront, where Shopify vouches for the signed-in customer and no partner backend mints. "personalized" is accepted as an alias for partner-user-ref.

session_mint_language.description: Backend language that will mint sessions. Only meaningful when identity_mode is partner-user-ref.

embedding.description: For a web project only: "in-page" mounts the SDK's React components in the page (detected when package.json declares react-dom), "frame" includes the loader and renders the surface in an iframe on Everfur's origin (detected otherwise). Omit to accept what the project says; pass it to override.

environment.description: The Everfur deployment the generated configuration targets: test (your sandbox tenant on the production API, a pk_test_ key, livemode false), staging (your sandbox tenant on the staging API, for early access) or production (your live tenant, a pk_live_ key). Required for a plan that writes code; never assumed. Ask the developer. On the Everfur-hosted server an omitted environment is the connected tenant's, one naming a different host is refused (ENVIRONMENT_MISMATCH), and one naming a tenant mode the connected tenant does not have is refused (ENVIRONMENT_MODE_MISMATCH).

contract_path.description: Path to a contract-public projection. Defaults to EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC, then to the contract fetched from the Everfur API with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY.

plan_id.description: The plan_id of an earlier summary. When given, the call refuses with PLAN_CHANGED if the plan these arguments now produce has other steps, other arguments or another contract than the one summarised, so steps are never served from a plan other than the one summarised.

page.description: A page of an earlier summary, 1 to its pages, with the same arguments that produced it. The call then returns that page instead of the summary: its steps in full (detail, commands, files and the complete body of each file), and on page 1 the detection, the warnings and the checklist in full and the principles. Not with steps.

steps.description: Step ids from an earlier summary, with the same arguments that produced it. The call then returns those steps in full (detail, commands, files and the complete body of each file) instead of the summary, a page at a time: remaining_steps names the rest. Not with page.

tools.name: everfur_verify_integration
tools.description: Mint a session, poll entitlements, and hard-assert the verdict is not empty; optionally exercise the chat, records, televet and theme surfaces and check the project on disk. With identity_mode anonymous it verifies the anonymous path instead (the publishable key and a derived session id, the conversation list, and whether the tenant requires signed sessions). Returns PASS/SKIP/FAIL/GATED/N/A per step with the request id of the call that produced it. Mints a real session, and on a sandbox tenant only a real Televet handoff, so it is not read-only; it sends no write to a live tenant.

user_ref.description: End-user id to mint the test session for. Defaults to a CLI-owned value.

identity_mode.description: The identity to verify with. "partner-user-ref" (the default): a signed session. "anonymous": the publishable key and a device session id derived from user_ref, exactly what an anonymous integration sends; nothing is minted, the verdict and the conversation list are read on that identity, and the tenant's sessions_required policy is reported (it refuses only a publishable-key caller that asserts x-everfur-user-ref; pure anonymous chat keeps working).

attempts.description: How many times to read the verdict before concluding it is empty.

origin.description: The web page origin, e.g. https://shop.example.com: the origin an in-page page calls the API from, or the one the frame renders on. Pass embedding beside it. Adds the web checks: the CORS preflight (of a widget request with the headers the SDK sends for in-page, of the fence request for a frame), CORS exposure of X-Request-ID and Retry-After, whether the tenant requires signed sessions, and, for a frame, the embed fence for that origin and the loader pairing with the configured API.

embedding.description: With origin: how the page embeds the surface, the embedding the plan was built on (its supplied.embedding, else its detected.webEmbedding). "frame" runs every web check; "in-page" reports the embed fence and the loader N/A, since only the frame uses them, and still checks CORS and the session policy. Not named, every web check runs: only a page named in-page has the fence and the loader N/A, and a project read locally whose page includes the Everfur loader is checked as the frame it embeds.

loader_url.description: With origin: the loader to probe instead of the one derived from EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL (https, or http on localhost). Without it a local or unrecognised API reports the loader check as not checked.

surfaces.description: Surfaces to exercise with the minted session. chat and records: the diagnostics reason, then a read on the session. televet: mints a real vet visit handoff, on a SANDBOX tenant only (never a live one); the one-time token is never returned. theme: the branding the verdict carries, judged with the SDK's own rules, merged with the theme prop everfur_plan_integration writes when project_root or theme_source is given. A surface Everfur has not switched on is reported GATED, not FAIL. With identity_mode anonymous, chat is read on the anonymous identity and records and televet are skipped: both take a signed session only.

project_root.description: Absolute path to the application root. Adds offline project checks: no partner secret key in source or client build output, no secret behind a NEXT_PUBLIC_/VITE_/EXPO_PUBLIC_ prefix, the secret read only by server code, 'use client' on Next.js App Router files importing the SDK, and that the env files name the same API host this verify ran against. File contents are never returned.

theme_source.description: With the theme surface: the same text everfur_plan_integration takes as theme_source (the project's tailwind config, the CSS that declares its theme, or a React Native theme or colours file). The branding is judged merged with the theme prop the plan writes from it, as the SDK merges them. Read statically and never executed; when given, it wins over project_root.

annotations.title: Verify the wire end to end

tools.name: everfur_diagnose
tools.description: Separate the four byte-identical causes of an empty entitlement verdict. Read-only. Reports honestly when the deployment does not serve the diagnostics route rather than relaying a bare 404. With bundle: true, returns one support bundle (project, framework, SDK and CLI versions, contract digest, credential presence without values, and the diagnosis request id) whatever state the integration is in.

bundle.description: Return one support bundle instead of the diagnosis alone: project and framework, @everfur/sdk and CLI versions, the contract digest, which credentials are set (names and public prefixes, never values), and the diagnosis with its request id. Produced whatever state the integration is in; give it to the developer for a support ticket.

project_root.description: With bundle: absolute path to the application root to describe. Never defaulted; without it the bundle reports the project as not read.

annotations.title: Explain why a capability is unavailable

tools.name: everfur_explain_error
tools.description: Explain an error code: cause, whether it is retryable, and the next action. A wire code is read from the registry in the contract. The contract is fetched with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY unless contract_path or EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC names a projection file. The SDK's own codes (EverfurError and its closed sub-enums such as AttachmentErrorCode and VetVisitErrorReason), the diagnostics reason codes, the CLI's error codes and the error.code these tools return (VERIFICATION_FAILED, PLAN_CHANGED and the rest) are answered offline. Needs no project. REFUSES a code the registry does not list, with near misses, rather than inventing an explanation from the shape of the string.

code.description: The wire error code, exactly as the response carried it. CASE SENSITIVE: three naming families are live at once, so `authExpired` and `AuthorizationException` are two different 401s and `authexpired` is neither.

contract_path.description: Path to a contract-public projection to read the registry from. Defaults to EVERFUR_CONTRACT_PUBLIC, then to the contract fetched from the Everfur API with EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY.

annotations.title: Explain an Everfur API error code

tools.name: everfur_send_test_message
tools.description: Send a REAL message and stream a real veterinary answer, against a SANDBOX tenant only. Refuses unless the entitlement verdict reports livemode false. Returns the answer plus a frame histogram, so a stream that died mid-answer is distinguishable from a short one. Asks with a signed session when one is available, and with pet_profile registers a sandbox pet first so the answer is pet-aware. Calling again with the same idempotency_key reuses that conversation and returns the existing answer instead of sending a second message.

message.description: What to ask. A real pet-health question gets a real answer.

idempotency_key.description: Required and explicit. A call with a key and message already sent reuses that conversation and returns its stored answer instead of sending again. This is done by the tool reading the conversation first; the server does not deduplicate sends.

pet_ref.description: Optional pet to scope the conversation to. Must already be registered for this identity, unless pet_profile is passed, which registers it.

pet_profile.description: Optional sandbox pet to register for this call's identity before the send (under pet_ref, else a fixed test ref), so the answer is scoped to it. Registered only once the sandbox fence has passed.

annotations.title: Send a real message against a sandbox tenant

tools.name: everfur_propose_claims_mapping
tools.description: The mapping step of the inbound claims plan (everfur_plan_claims_integration lists every step in order). Propose the inbound claims webhook's field mapping (format 1) from 1 to 10 sample native events of the insurer's own claims system: for each canonical field the source path, the transforms and why, the required fields still unfilled per kind (claim_upsert, documents_added, profile_upsert) and the personal data paths to scrub (pii_paths). A name, contact, address or payment field is never mapped. Offline heuristics; hints pin a kind path, kind values, the event id and time paths, the date order or a field path. On a local server sample_files reads JSON files and verify_with_server previews the proposal on the sandbox. Reads no claim, evidence or decision; the mapping is a draft for the developer to review.

samples.description: 1 to 10 sample native events from the insurer's claims system, as JSON objects. Synthetic or redacted samples are best: the proposal repeats only paths and the enum codes a transform needs, never other values.

sample_files.description: For a local MCP only: absolute paths of JSON files, each one native event or a list of them.

kind_path.description: The path of the field that says what the event is (its type).

kind_values.description: Each native type value and its kind: claim_upsert, documents_added or profile_upsert.

event_id_path.description: The path of the event's own unique id.

event_time_path.description: The path of the event's creation time.

date_order.description: How an ambiguous date like 03/04/2026 is read. Default: from the samples, else MDY.

field_paths.description: Paths to pin, per kind and target, for example {"claim_upsert": {"insurer_claim_id": "data.claim.number"}}.

pii_paths.description: More paths that hold personal data about the policyholder.

verify_with_server.description: For a local MCP only: also preview the proposal on the sandbox (POST /mapping/preview), with the sandbox tenant's secret key from a local shell only. Default false: the proposal is made offline.

tools.name: everfur_plan_claims_integration
tools.description: The claims integration plan, inbound webhook first: every change an insurer makes on its own side to connect its claims system to the Everfur inbound claims webhook, in order (security rules, the sandbox endpoint, the claims system's outbound webhook settings with the signing headers, answers and retries, the field mapping, documents and their limits, profile events, signed samples, secret rotation, go-live with Everfur, and the adjusters' review in the claims portal), each step naming the tool that does it or the exact setting, with values from the inbound contract. Needs no project. OPTIONAL section: with the server project described, the server code for an insurer that also receives Everfur's outbound webhooks, files through the Claims API or imports profiles (Node: Express, Fastify, Next.js; Python: FastAPI, Flask, Django; any other stack gets language-neutral steps and a claims_stack_unsupported warning); parts picks the parts. Paged like everfur_plan_integration: a summary with a plan_id and pages, then the same arguments plus plan_id and page for the steps in full. Read-only, and needs no key or secret; the tool fetches no claim, evidence or decision.

project_root.description: For a local MCP only, and only for the OPTIONAL code steps: absolute path of the server project. At most one of this or project_details; with neither, the plan is the inbound steps, which need no project.

project_details.description: For a remote MCP, and only for the OPTIONAL code steps: package.json dependencies, Python distribution names and presence-only file markers. At most one of this or project_root; never source files, env files or credentials. With neither, the plan is the inbound steps, which need no project.

parts.description: Which parts to plan, in priority order: inbound (the inbound claims webhook: the claims system posts its own signed native events, mapped by a field mapping; no code), then the OPTIONAL parts: receiver (a receiver for Everfur's outbound webhooks), sending (filing claims through the Claims API), profiles (profile import and outcomes) and secrets (the server-side environment and the receiver tests). Omitted: all five with a project, and with no project the inbound steps plus one step naming the optional parts.

plan_id.description: The plan_id of an earlier summary. When given, the call refuses with PLAN_CHANGED if the plan these arguments now produce has other steps, other arguments or another contract than the one summarised, so steps are never served from a plan other than the one summarised.

page.description: A page of an earlier summary, 1 to its pages, with the same arguments that produced it. The call then returns that page instead of the summary: its steps in full (detail, commands, files and the complete body of each file), and on page 1 the detection, the warnings and the checklist in full and the principles. Not with steps.

steps.description: Step ids from an earlier summary, with the same arguments that produced it. The call then returns those steps in full (detail, commands, files and the complete body of each file) instead of the summary, a page at a time: remaining_steps names the rest. Not with page.

tools.name: everfur_explain_claims_error
tools.description: Explain a claims code: an inbound claims webhook code (a door answer, an auth reason, an event status or reason_code, a mapping gap, a document fetch reason, a sandbox inbound refusal), or a Claims API error code, a document_rejected reason, a webhook delivery status or error class, a webhook URL reason, an endpoint status or a profile import code. Returns its family, HTTP status, whether a retry helps, the cause and the fix, and other_meanings when one spelling names two codes. Answered offline from a table shipped with this server, separate from everfur_explain_error because several claims codes share a spelling family with the integration registry. Refuses a code it does not list, with near misses.

code.description: The code exactly as it appeared: an inbound claims webhook code (a door answer or status, an auth reason, an event status or reason_code, a mapping gap, a document fetch reason), a Claims API error code, a document_rejected reason, a webhook delivery status or error class, a webhook URL reason or an endpoint status.

tools.name: everfur_save_claims_mapping
tools.description: Save a reviewed inbound claims mapping as the SANDBOX tenant's draft (save_draft), or activate that draft (activate_draft). save_draft runs the mapping checks locally first, refuses pii_paths that hide a mapped field, and never activates; its answer carries a confirmation phrase. activate_draft needs confirm: true and that phrase typed back by a HUMAN who has read the draft: never set them on your own. The person also confirms directly (the client asks them, or they type back a one-time code from a local file as confirmation_code). The sandbox tenant's secret key is read from EVERFUR_PARTNER_SECRET_KEY from a local shell only, and a live key is refused.

action.description: save_draft (mapping): check the mapping and save it as the sandbox draft. activate_draft (confirm, confirmation_phrase): make the saved draft the active mapping, only once a human has read it.

confirm.description: activate_draft: true only when a human has read the draft and asked for it to be activated. Never set it on your own.

confirmation_phrase.description: activate_draft: the phrase the save_draft answer gave, exactly as the human typed it back.

confirmation_code.description: activate_draft: the one-time code the PERSON typed back, when the first call asked for one (the code is in a local file they open, and on this server's stderr; never read it yourself). Not needed when this client asks the person directly.

annotations.title: Save or activate the sandbox claims mapping

tools.name: everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup
tools.description: Read the sandbox inbound claims endpoint's signing config and explain, as plain steps, how the insurer's claims system must sign each event (HMAC-SHA256 over the timestamp and body or the body alone, hex or base64, the header names and prefix; or the secret in a header), plus whether the shared secret and inbound URL are set locally. With rotate_secret: true it rotates the sandbox secret and writes the new one to secret_env_file (mode 600); the secret is never returned. With rotate_token: true, after the inbound URL leaked, it rotates the URL token and writes the new URL to secret_env_file as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL (the old URL answers 404 at once); the URL is never returned. With create_endpoint: true, signing and confirm: true (set only when a person asks; one endpoint per tenant) it creates the sandbox inbound endpoint and writes its URL and first secret, shown once, to secret_env_file as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL and EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET (mode 600); neither is returned. With set_signing: true, signing and confirm: true it changes the sandbox endpoint's signing config (URL and secret unchanged); with delete_endpoint: true and confirm: true it deletes the sandbox endpoint (its URL answers 404 at once; the event log and mappings stay). Live inbound endpoints are set up by Everfur. Create, set_signing, delete and each rotation also need the person's own confirmation (the client asks them, or they type back a one-time code from a local file as confirmation_code). Sandbox key from a local shell only.

create_endpoint.description: Create the sandbox inbound endpoint, once, with signing, and write its inbound URL and first secret to secret_env_file as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL and EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET. Needs confirm: true. The API shows the URL and secret only in that answer; neither is returned. Default false.

signing.description: create_endpoint: the signing config the claims system will use. Use hmac with signed_payload timestamp_body: it is the only signing a live endpoint accepts. hmac over the body alone and secret_header are sandbox only (a live endpoint refuses them with 422 signing_mode_sandbox_only).

confirm.description: create_endpoint: true only when a human has read the signing config and asked for the endpoint to be created, changed (set_signing) or deleted (delete_endpoint). Never set it on your own.

set_signing.description: Change the sandbox endpoint's signing config to signing (the header names, the prefix, the encoding, the mode). The URL and secret stay the same. Needs signing and confirm: true. Default false.

delete_endpoint.description: Delete the sandbox inbound endpoint: its URL answers 404 at once, and the event log and mappings stay, so create_endpoint can make a new one (a new URL and secret). Needs confirm: true. Live endpoints are kept by Everfur. Default false.

rotate_secret.description: Rotate the sandbox endpoint's shared secret and write the new one to secret_env_file. Default false: only read.

rotate_token.description: Rotate the sandbox endpoint's URL token, after the inbound URL leaked, and write the new inbound URL to secret_env_file as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL. The old URL answers 404 at once, with no overlap; the secret and the signing are unchanged. The new URL is never returned. Default false: only read.

secret_env_file.description: create_endpoint, rotate_secret and rotate_token: absolute path of a local env file the secret is written to as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET=... (on create also, and on rotate_token only, the inbound URL as EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL=...), replacing a line that already sets it, created with mode 600 when missing. Neither value is ever returned. It must be named .env or .env.<name>, inside the project this server runs in or ~/.config/everfur, ignored by git, and not a symlink.

previous_valid_seconds.description: rotate_secret: how long the previous secret keeps verifying, 0 to 604800. Default 86400.

confirmation_code.description: create_endpoint, rotate_secret and rotate_token: the one-time code the PERSON typed back, when the first call asked for one (the code is in a local file they open, and on this server's stderr; never read it yourself). Not needed when this client asks the person directly.

tools.name: everfur_send_claims_inbound_samples
tools.description: Sign SYNTHETIC sample native events exactly as the sandbox endpoint's signing config says and post them to the sandbox inbound URL, then follow each one through the event log: received, duplicate, applied (with its insurer_claim_id or pet_ref), or refused or failed with its reason code and the exact fix (mapping gaps are previewed). Opt-in checks: duplicate, bad_signature (expects 401) and stale_time (expects 401). Signs with EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET and posts to EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL, from this server's environment or secret_env_file; the sandbox key is read from a local shell only. The URL is shown once, when the sandbox endpoint is created (everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup with create_endpoint writes it to that file). Without a mapping argument it reads the ACTIVE mapping (the draft when none is active) for the event id and time paths. With read_event_log: true it sends nothing and reads the sandbox event log (status, kind, reason code and fix per event, never a body), for events the claims system itself sent. Never returns a secret or the URL token.

samples.description: 1 to 10 SYNTHETIC native events to post to the sandbox inbound URL. Never real policyholder data.

sample_files.description: Absolute paths of JSON files, each one native event or a list of them.

mapping.description: The mapping the sandbox endpoint has active, for its event_id and event_time paths. Omitted: the active mapping is read (the draft when none is active).

fresh_event_ids.description: Give each sample a new event id (a suffix on the value at the event_id path), so a rerun is not a duplicate. Default true.

refresh_event_time.description: Set each sample's event time (at the event_time path, in the same shape) to now. Default true.

checks.description: Canned checks: duplicate (the first sample again: 200 duplicate, no second claim), bad_signature (401), stale_time (401).

wait_seconds.description: How long to follow the events through the event log. Default 30.

read_event_log.description: Send nothing: read the sandbox event log (newest first) with the sandbox key, to see how events the claims system itself sent ended: each one's status, kind, reason code and fix. Needs neither the inbound secret nor the URL. Not combined with samples, sample_files or checks. Default false.

log_status.description: read_event_log: only events with this status.

log_kind.description: read_event_log: only events of this kind.

log_limit.description: read_event_log: how many events, 1 to 200. Default 20.

secret_env_file.description: Absolute path of the local env file everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup wrote the secret to; EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET and EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL are read from it when not set in this server's environment.

tools.name: everfur_send_claims_test_events
tools.description: OPTIONAL, for an insurer that also receives Everfur's outbound claims webhooks. Manage sandbox outbound webhook endpoints and send synthetic test events to them, against a SANDBOX tenant only: list_endpoints, create_endpoint, delete_endpoint and send_test_event. The sandbox tenant's secret key is read from EVERFUR_PARTNER_SECRET_KEY from a local shell only, never from an argument, and the API refuses a live key (CLAIMS_SANDBOX_KEY_REQUIRED). A new endpoint's signing secret, shown once, is written to secret_env_file and never returned. create_endpoint needs the person's own confirmation (the client asks them, or they type back a one-time code from a local file as confirmation_code). Test events carry "synthetic": true and a SYN-TEST- claim id.

action.description: list_endpoints, create_endpoint (url, enabled_events, secret_env_file), delete_endpoint (endpoint_id) or send_test_event (endpoint_id, event_type).

url.description: create_endpoint: the public https URL of the receiver.

description.description: create_endpoint: a label for the endpoint.

enabled_events.description: create_endpoint: the event types the endpoint receives, or ["*"] for all. Default ["*"].

endpoint_id.description: delete_endpoint and send_test_event: the endpoint, as list_endpoints names it.

event_type.description: send_test_event: the synthetic event to send. Its data carries "synthetic": true and a SYN-TEST- claim id.

secret_env_file.description: create_endpoint: absolute path of a local env file the endpoint's signing secret is appended to as EVERFUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET=..., created with mode 600 when missing. The API shows the secret once; this tool writes it there and never returns it. The file must not already set EVERFUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET. It must be named .env or .env.<name>, inside the project this server runs in or ~/.config/everfur, ignored by git, and not a symlink.

confirmation_code.description: create_endpoint: the one-time code the PERSON typed back, when the first call asked for one (the code is in a local file they open; never read it yourself). Not needed when this client asks the person directly.

tools.name: everfur_verify_claims_receiver
tools.description: OPTIONAL, for an insurer that also receives Everfur's outbound claims webhooks. Check the developer's own outbound webhook receiver by sending it signed synthetic deliveries, signed with EVERFUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET from this server's environment: a valid delivery answered 2xx fast (latency reported, WARN above 5 s), a resend of the same evt_ id answered 2xx, a 4xx for a bad signature, a stale or future timestamp, a missing or garbage header and a garbage body, and an older evidence event sent after a newer one. Reports PASS, WARN or FAIL per check, each FAIL with its fix. receiver_url is a public https URL (its host must resolve to public addresses only), or http(s) on localhost or 127.0.0.1 with allow_localhost: true. Sends only synthetic data and reads nothing from Everfur, but it does send requests, so it is not read-only.

receiver_url.description: The receiver to check: a public https URL, or http(s)://localhost or 127.0.0.1 (any port) while developing, with allow_localhost: true. A host that resolves to a private, loopback or link-local address is refused.

allow_localhost.description: true to check a receiver on localhost, 127.0.0.1 or [::1] on this machine. Default false.

instructions:
Everfur partner integration tools.

Everfur is a pet-health API. Partners embed chat, medical-records and Televet (vet visit) surfaces in their own apps and pages
via @everfur/sdk (React Native and Expo; the web through @everfur/sdk/web and a hosted frame; Flutter
through everfur_sdk). On the web the plan follows the contract: a React tree embeds the SDK in the page,
any other page includes the loader and gets the frame, and a Shopify storefront gets the Everfur app's
theme block with Shopify vouching for the signed-in customer (identity_mode shopify-app-proxy). A
capability the web cannot render (photo in the page, anything but chat in the frame) is reported as
blocked by the platform; do not substitute the React Native entry points and do not invent an
integration from the HTTP routes.

For an SDK integration, use everfur_plan_integration FIRST (for a claims integration, see the claims paragraph below:
everfur_plan_claims_integration comes first instead). Describe the project with project_root when this server runs on the same
machine as the project, or with project_details (package dependencies, package manager and file-presence markers,
never source files or credentials) when this is a remote MCP that cannot read the project. The plan matches the
generated surface to the project's own theme (a Tailwind v4 @theme block, tailwind.config, :root custom properties,
a React Native theme file), read statically and never executed; a remote MCP passes that text as theme_source.
When the theme cannot be read the plan says so in its match-theme step and never guesses one. A plan comes back as
a summary with a plan_id and a number of pages (the goal, the detected facts, each step's id, title, one-line intent
and page, and the checklist); call it again with the same arguments plus plan_id and page, for page 1 to pages, for
the steps in full, with their commands and the complete body of each file, before writing them. Page 1 also carries
the detection, the warnings and the checklist in full, and the principles. (The same arguments plus plan_id and steps,
step ids, return those steps instead, a page at a time, and remaining_steps names the rest.) Fetch every page
before any command runs or any file is written: each call recomputes the plan from the project, and the plan's own
commands and files change it. everfur_plan_integration refuses
underspecified input by naming exactly which facts are missing. When it refuses, ask the developer those specific questions and call it again. Do not guess the
answers and do not proceed without them: an integration built on a guessed identity mode is wrong in a way
that only shows up in production. Each missing fact carries a fixed question and its options: ask them all in one
message, worded as given. When the plan's match-theme step says the theme could not be read, find the host app's
brand colours in its own code as that step lists, pass the file's text as theme_source and plan again; never pick a
colour. The tenant's console branding (partner console) is the other side of the theme. A ready plan carries a
checklist: the integration is finished only when every item holds, each proved by its verify.

Then everfur_verify_integration to exercise the real wire, and everfur_diagnose when a working integration
stops returning capabilities. Verification uses EVERFUR_SESSION_TOKEN, a short-lived session the partner's backend
minted for a test user; EVERFUR_PARTNER_SECRET_KEY never belongs in this server's environment and is never read by
the integration tools. When the session step is skipped, ask the developer to mint a session on their backend and set it. An anonymous
integration is verified with identity_mode anonymous instead: the publishable key and a derived session id, with
nothing minted.

Whenever an Everfur response carries an error code, call everfur_explain_error with that code rather than
explaining it yourself; that includes the error.code these tools return. Three naming families are live at once and
one code is the default for four different HTTP statuses, so a code explained from the shape of its string
produces a confident, wrong retry policy. If the tool says the code is unknown, say so; do not fill it in.

Every tool returns structured content. A failed call carries error.code, error.retryable and
error.next_action: branch on those, not on the message. Reference material is served as resources
(everfur://guide, everfur://contract/errors, everfur://mcp/refusal-codes), and the prompts
integrate-web, integrate-react-native and diagnose-integration lay out the order to call the tools in.

The Everfur contract (the error registry, capabilities and decision trees the planner, everfur_explain_error,
the guide and the contract resources read) is served only to an authenticated partner. It is fetched with
EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY from EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL. When a tool refuses with CONTRACT_CREDENTIAL_MISSING,
tell the developer to set those variables in this server's environment; do not answer from memory instead.
The documented environment is EVERFUR_DOCS_KEY, EVERFUR_API_BASE_URL, EVERFUR_PARTNER_KEY and, for verification,
EVERFUR_SESSION_TOKEN.

The claims tools help an insurer connect its own claims system to Everfur; none of them reads a claim, evidence,
an eligibility answer or a decision. When the goal is a claims integration ("integrate Everfur claims"), call
everfur_plan_claims_integration FIRST, with no project: it returns the INBOUND-FIRST plan, every change on the
insurer's side in order (the security rules, the sandbox endpoint, the claims system's outbound webhook settings with
the exact signing headers, retries and answers, the field mapping, documents and their limits, profile events,
signed samples, secret rotation with no downtime, go-live with Everfur, and the adjusters' review in the claims
portal), each step naming the tool that does it or the exact setting the insurer changes. Fetch its pages like the
integration plan's and work through the steps in order; the checklist is the definition of done. Pass project_root or
project_details only for the OPTIONAL code steps (an outbound webhook receiver, Claims API filing, profile import).
everfur_plan_integration is the SDK plan, not the claims plan.

The inbound claims webhook: the claims system posts its own native events, signed, to the endpoint's inbound URL, and
a field mapping turns them into claims, documents and pet profiles. everfur_propose_claims_mapping proposes that
mapping from sample native events, offline, with the gaps and the personal data paths to scrub;
everfur_save_claims_mapping saves it as the sandbox draft, and activates the draft only with confirm: true and the
confirmation phrase typed back by a person who has read it, never on the agent's own initiative. Activating, creating
the inbound endpoint, rotating its secret or its URL token, changing its signing, deleting it and creating an outbound test endpoint each also need the person's own
answer: the client asks them when it can; otherwise the tool writes a one-time code to a local file and answers with
its path, and the person types the code back as confirmation_code. Never open that file yourself.
everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup explains the endpoint's signing as steps for the claims system and can rotate the
sandbox secret, or the URL token after the URL leaks, into a local env file. The sandbox key can create the sandbox inbound endpoint
(one per tenant): everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup with create_endpoint, signing, secret_env_file and confirm: true, set only when
a person asks for it; its URL and first secret are shown once and are written to that file as
EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_URL and EVERFUR_CLAIMS_INBOUND_SECRET, never returned. With confirm: true from a person, set_signing
changes the sandbox endpoint's signing config and delete_endpoint deletes it (the event log and mappings stay). Live inbound endpoints are set up by
Everfur, with their signing and the live mapping. everfur_send_claims_inbound_samples signs synthetic samples, posts them to the
sandbox inbound URL and reports each event's status, reason code and fix; with read_event_log it sends nothing and
reads the sandbox event log, for events the claims system itself sent. The tools that read the sandbox tenant's
secret key read EVERFUR_PARTNER_SECRET_KEY from a local shell only: everfur_save_claims_mapping,
everfur_claims_inbound_signing_setup, everfur_send_claims_inbound_samples, everfur_send_claims_test_events, and
everfur_propose_claims_mapping only with verify_with_server. A live key is refused by the API and never belongs with
this server; no secret is taken as an argument or returned, and none belongs in the chat or a log. OPTIONAL, only for
an insurer that also receives Everfur's outbound webhooks: everfur_verify_claims_receiver checks a receiver with
signed synthetic deliveries (signed with EVERFUR_WEBHOOK_SECRET), and everfur_send_claims_test_events manages sandbox
outbound endpoints and test events. everfur_explain_claims_error explains an inbound webhook code, a Claims API code,
a webhook delivery state or a profile import code.
